## New Features

- The opt-in terminal workspace supports multiple side-chat tabs. Switch between them with the keyboard or mouse, and reopen saved local side chats after restarting Codex. (#59784, #60152, #60181)
- Search older tasks from the agent command center by name, prompt preview, or working directory. (#60286)
- Turn on **Collapse turn details** in the full-screen transcript to fold completed activity beneath each prompt while keeping answers visible and tool output searchable. (#60554, #60555, #60556, #60557)
- Add or edit custom model providers from the terminal. With custom gateway onboarding enabled, you can create a provider during sign-in and use a device code for supported gateways over SSH or without a local browser. (#59779, #60009, #60186, #60486, #60662)
- Press `Ctrl+S` in the terminal report editor to save a diagnostic ZIP locally, even when uploads are disabled. (#60542)
- With the opt-in Cloud connection on macOS and Linux, send images, choose a model and reasoning effort, and archive or restore Cloud conversations from the terminal. (#59828, #60061, #60635, #60651)

## Bug Fixes

- `codex exec` keeps project configuration and MCP servers disabled in untrusted directories, even with `--sandbox workspace-write`. Use `--trust` with `codex exec` or `codex review` to explicitly save project trust. (#60041)
- **Yes, clear context and implement** now hands the full approved plan to the fresh session and keeps the current session open if the handoff fails. (#60763)
- Fixed Windows sandbox handling for quoted `cmd.exe` paths and for PowerShell sessions whose

## Core

### Bugfixes
- Failed TUI worker requests now return an error instead of leaving the caller hanging. (@Nowaker)

**Thank you to 1 community contributor:**
- @Nowaker:
  - fix(opencode): answer a failed TUI worker request instead of hanging (#54936)

### New Features

- **Fork sessions whose folder is gone**: when a session's original folder was moved or deleted, you can now fork it into the current folder instead of only continuing, so later resumes no longer ask. See [Continue or switch sessions](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.5.2/packages/coding-agent/docs/sessions.md#continue-or-switch-sessions).

### Changed

- When a session's working directory no longer exists, for example after the project folder was renamed, interactive mode now offers `Continue`, `Fork`, or `Cancel` instead of only continuing. `Continue` runs the session in the current directory without storing the choice, as before; `Fork` copies it into the current directory as a new session with a new ID, like `--fork`, so the next resume no longer asks. This applies at startup (`--session`, `--resume`), to `/resume`, to `/import`, and to `ctx.switchSession()` from extensions ([#11975](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), fixes [#11060](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))

### Fixed

- Fixed `/import` of a session whose working directory no longer exists leaving a copy in the session directory, and continuing it leaving a second copy with the same ID (`s.jsonl` and `s-1.jsonl`); the failed copy is now removed ([#11975](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11975) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), fixes [#11060](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11060))
- Fixed Anthropic OAuth requests reporting an outdated Claude Code version

# Skill toggles, tool timers and a faster Hyper ⚡ This release was brought to you by our team and our favorite contributors! Long awaited features ahead, read along! ## Toggle skills Skills can now be switched on and off right from the command palette. Broken skills are easy to spot, too! (they're marked with a red × and the reason they failed) ## 🕐 How long is this taking? Every tool call now shows how long it's been running. Now, you'll know whether that test suite is just slow or actually stuck. ## Lighter, faster Hyper ⚡ Requests to Hyper are now compressed with [Brotli](https://brotli.org/) 🥦. That means much smaller uploads on every turn and snappier responses, especially in long sessions. Hyper now also supports [Gzip](https://www.gzip.org/) that other agents could use when Brotli if not viable. Big thanks to @BrunoKrugel for the first 2 awesome features! ## 🖇️  Connect your Claude Pro or Max subscription

If you have a Claude Pro or Max subscription, Plandex can use it when calling Anthropic models. You can use it in either Integrated Models Mode on Plandex Cloud, or in BYO Key Mode (whether on Cloud or self-hosting).

Assuming you're using Anthropic models (which the default model pack does), you'll be asked if you want to connect your Claude subscription the first time you run Plandex. Follow the instructions to connect.

[Learn more in the docs.](https://docs.plandex.ai/models/claude-subscription)

`pip install 'browser-use==1.0.5'`

- Every run is judged by your own model: one more low-effort request checks the run against the task and fills `result.judgement` with `success`, `failure_reason`, `description`, `prompt_injection_detected`, `bot_block_or_captcha_detected` and `gotchas`. `judge_context=` gives it your criteria; `judge=False` turns it off; the 0.x `use_judge` / `ground_truth` work again (#6398).
- The judge sees the trace, the run's last screenshots and the final page (unless `use_vision=False`). It writes gotchas whenever the site rejected input, errored, blocked or rate-limited the agent, also on a successful run, e.g. "The form requires phone numbers in (###) ###-#### format" (#6403).

13 real runs, each judged 3 times: gotchas on 15/15 verdicts where the site pushed back (6/15 before), 2/24 on clean runs, success verdicts unchanged.

# Nanobrowser v0.3.0

Nanobrowser 0.3 is rebuilt from the ground up: one agent in the side panel, on top of a new browser control layer that clicks the right element, acts like a real user and reports what really happened.

## What's new

- **CDP.** The new browser control is rebuilt with chrome.debugger API, it uses CDP to interact with elements in web pages. It's more stable than the previous injected scripts solution.
- **One agent, one chat per tab.** The old planner and navigator are replaced by a single agent. Several tasks can run side by side, each in its own tab group.
- **You decide what it may do.** Ask mode (default) asks before the agent submits, sends, deletes or uploads; Auto mode goes ahead. Payments, passwords, codes and access grants are always handed to you. Set any site to Allow, Ask or Block.
- **More reliable actions.** Each element has an ID tied to that exact element, clicks and typing are real browser input, and every action is sent once and reports whether the page responded.
- **Any model with tool calling.** Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Grok, DeepSeek, Mistral, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama and LM Studio. Pick the model and reasoning effort per chat; Test models in Settings checks which ones work.
- **Attachments and uploads.** Attach images, text files or a screenshot of the tab; the agent can upload your files to a page and save results (CSV, Markdown) to Downloads.
- **Shortcuts, voice and custom instructions.** Start saved prompts with `/`, speak with OpenAI's or Gemini's voice model, and tell the agent what to

## Highlights

### Resumable Agent streams (now for every Agent)
Every `Agent` can now publish a resumable run stream with replay caching, cross-instance observe/abort (`agent.observe(runId)`, `observe().abort()`, `agent.abortRunStream(runId)`), and ownership/TTL enforcement—so clients can reconnect without killing the run by default.

### Built-in MCP server at `/api/mcp` + OAuth discovery
`@mastra/server` now ships a built-in MCP endpoint (enabled by default when `server.auth` is configured) so MCP clients can call your agents/workflows/tools without defining an `MCPServer`, plus OAuth discovery/audience checks via `server.mcp.oauth` and a new introspection route `GET /api/mcp/builtin`.

### Workflow Storage Version 2 (delta writes) now supported on Postgres + libSQL
Experimental `storageVersion: 2` reduces writes by persisting only per-step changes (instead of rewriting the whole run) and now works with `@mastra/pg` and `@mastra/libsql`, with results that can lazily load step history via an async `steps()` function.

### Resumable AI SDK chat routes (`useChat({ resume: true })` support)
`chatRoute({ resumable: true })` now generates a POST + reconnect GET endpoint pair that replays/follows active runs via `agent.observe(runId)`, with explicit route-array configuration support (`server.apiRoutes: [routes]`).

### One-off and bounded schedules for agents & workflows
Schedules now support one-time execution (`runAt`) and bounded recurring execution (`endAt`), with TypeScript updates (`cron` is optional) across server, client, and multiple storage backends.

### 🧭 Classify and Route with the OpenAI Decisions API
Three new components use the OpenAI Decisions API to choose how to handle your data without instructions. [`OpenAIDecisionsTextRouter`](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/openaidecisionstextrouter) sends text to a named output per label, [`OpenAIDecisionsImageRouter`](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/openaidecisionsimagerouter) does the same for images and can send low-confidence decisions to a fallback branch, and [`OpenAIDecisionsDocumentClassifier`](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/openaidecisionsdocumentclassifier) answers choice, score, and yes/no questions about documents and stores the answers in their metadata.

```python
from haystack.components.routers import OpenAIDecisionsTextRouter

router = OpenAIDecisionsTextRouter(
    labels={
        "billing": "Payments, invoices, refunds and charges",
        "technical": "Bugs, crashes and errors in the product",
    },
    instructions="Which team should handle this support request?",
    min_confidence=0.6,
)

print(router.run(text="I was charged twice for my subscription."))
# >> {'billing': 'I was charged twice for my subscription.'}
```

# Agent Zero — Release Notes

## Highlights

This is a large release that promotes core tools into standalone plugins, overhauls the welcome screen, hardens channel security, improves streaming and UI responsiveness, and adds new search, migration, and documentation capabilities.

---

## Tool Plugin Architecture

- **Extracted bundled tools into standalone plugins:** `wait`, `notify_user`, `search_engine`, `a2a_chat`, `scheduler`, `behavior_adjustment`, and the scheduler Tasks UI are now standard plugins, each with dedicated badge styling, log types, and prompt files.
- **Unified memory tools:** The four separate `memory_load`, `memory_save`, `memory_delete`, and `memory_forget` tools are consolidated into a single `memory` tool with an `action` argument, matching the action-dispatch pattern used by other tools.
- **Per-action tool permissions:** Profiles can now allow or deny individual operations across all 12 bundled multi-action tools (e.g., allow file reads but block writes, or allow listing scheduled tasks but block deletion). The Agent Editor shows grouped action controls with expandable entries.
- **Centralized boolean argument coercion** across all promoted and core tools, removing duplicated helpers and strict-validation error paths.
- **Dedicated badge rendering** for goal, document_query, skills, vision, browser, office, and computer_use_remote tool calls, each with distinct accent colors and descriptive headlines.
- **Dropped agent-name prefix** from all tool log headlines, warning rows, and fallback entries for cleaner chat output.
- **Added catalog thumbnail
